rules.quote: Classes and methods must be either **Integrations** or **Operations** — never both.
rules.rule: Make each class and method either an Integration or an Operation, never both.

rules.quote: but do not call other project/solution methods
rules.rule: Do not make an Operation call other project or solution methods.

rules.quote: Using framework methods and third-party libraries is fine.
rules.rule: Operations may use framework methods and third-party libraries.

rules.quote: contain no considerable logic themselves
rules.rule: Do not put considerable logic inside an Integration method.

rules.quote: If a method contains considerable logic, it should not also call other project methods.
rules.rule: If a method contains considerable logic, do not make it call other project methods.

rules.quote: Integrations may contain trivial conditionals (simple routing, guard-style early returns)
rules.rule: Integrations may contain trivial conditionals such as simple routing or guard-style early returns.

rules.quote: Do not mix logic and composition in the same method — split them.
rules.rule: Do not mix logic and composition in the same method; split them into separate methods.

rules.quote: Operations are covered by focused unit tests.
rules.rule: Cover Operations with focused unit tests.

rules.quote: Integrations are covered by a small number of integration/wiring tests.
rules.rule: Cover Integrations with a small number of integration or wiring tests.

rules.quote: Write the simplest code that solves the current, actual problem.
rules.rule: Write the simplest code that solves the current, actual problem.

rules.quote: Do not add abstractions, generics, or extension points for hypothetical future requirements.
rules.rule: Do not add abstractions, generics, or extension points for hypothetical future requirements.

rules.quote: Do not design for reusability if something is used in only one place.
rules.rule: Do not design for reusability when something is used in only one place.

rules.quote: Do not make things configurable if a constant works for now
rules.rule: Do not make things configurable when a constant works for now.

rules.quote: Do not add parameters, interfaces, or indirection that serve no present purpose.
rules.rule: Do not add parameters, interfaces, or indirection that serve no present purpose.

rules.quote: should be functionally pure
rules.rule: Make domain logic functionally pure: same inputs produce same outputs with no side effects.

rules.quote: It must not depend on I/O (no file access, no network calls, no UI interaction, no randomness/time unless injected).
rules.rule: Do not make domain logic depend on I/O, file access, network calls, UI interaction, or uninjected randomness or time.

rules.quote: are isolated at the edges of the system
rules.rule: Isolate I/O concerns at the edges of the system.

rules.quote: inject it as a parameter rather than reading it inside the logic
rules.rule: When domain logic needs an external value such as the current time, inject it as a parameter instead of reading it inside the logic.

rules.quote: Domain logic and I/O concerns must not be mixed.
rules.rule: Do not mix domain logic and I/O concerns.

rules.quote: Do not pass function call results or newly constructed objects directly as arguments to methods.
rules.rule: Do not pass function call results or newly constructed objects directly as method arguments.

rules.quote: Assign to a named variable first.
rules.rule: Assign a function call result or newly constructed object to a named variable before passing it as an argument.

rules.quote: This rule does not apply to test code.
rules.rule: The no-inline-construction rule does not apply to test code.

rules.quote: Use comments sparingly, if at all.
rules.rule: Use comments sparingly, if at all.

rules.quote: The reasoning behind a decision belongs in the git commit message, not inline.
rules.rule: Put the reasoning behind a decision in the git commit message, not in code comments.

rules.quote: first rename the method/class/variable so the name itself carries that meaning
rules.rule: When a comment feels needed, first rename the method, class, or variable so the name carries that meaning.

rules.quote: only if no name can express it does a comment earn its place
rules.rule: Write a comment only if no name can express the meaning.

rules.quote: Doc-block summaries restating a well-named function's behavior
rules.rule: Do not write doc-block summaries that restate a well-named function's behavior.

rules.quote: module-header prose explaining the domain
rules.rule: Do not write module-header prose explaining the domain.

rules.quote: Never reference issue-tracker items or ADR/decision documents in code comments
rules.rule: Never reference issue-tracker items or ADR/decision documents in code comments.

rules.quote: Never reference issue-tracker items or ADR/decision documents in commit messages
rules.rule: Never reference issue-tracker items or ADR/decision documents in commit messages.

rules.quote: before writing any comment, try to express it via renaming instead
rules.rule: Before writing any comment, try to express it through renaming instead.

rules.quote: state it directly in its own words — never by pointing at an issue or ADR
rules.rule: If a constraint cannot live in a name, state it directly in its own words, never by pointing at an issue or ADR.

rules.quote: Review the diff for accumulated doc blocks before reporting.
rules.rule: Review the diff for accumulated doc blocks before reporting.

rules.quote: Only validate and handle errors at **system boundaries**
rules.rule: Only validate and handle errors at system boundaries such as user input, external APIs, file I/O, and network calls.

rules.quote: **Do not** add defensive checks inside internal code that is already guaranteed correct by domain logic or the type system.
rules.rule: Do not add defensive checks inside internal code already guaranteed correct by domain logic or the type system.

rules.quote: do not add a null-check or guard just because the type system allows it in theory
rules.rule: If a null or invalid state is unreachable given domain invariants, do not add a null check or guard just because the type system allows it.

rules.quote: Do not add try/catch blocks, fallbacks, or error branches for conditions that cannot occur given the current call context.
rules.rule: Do not add try/catch blocks, fallbacks, or error branches for conditions that cannot occur in the current call context.

rules.quote: Trust framework and library guarantees
rules.rule: Trust framework and library guarantees.

rules.quote: do not re-validate what the framework already ensures
rules.rule: Do not re-validate what the framework already ensures.

rules.quote: Prefer letting unexpected failures propagate and crash loudly (fail-fast) rather than silently swallowing them with defensive code that hides bugs.
rules.rule: Prefer letting unexpected failures propagate and crash loudly (fail-fast) rather than silently swallowing them with defensive code.

rules.quote: One very short sentence describing **what** was done (the subject line).
rules.rule: Write the commit message subject as one very short sentence describing what was done.

rules.quote: A blank line.
rules.rule: Separate the commit message subject from the body with a blank line.

rules.quote: A short explanation of **why** the change was made (the body).
rules.rule: Write the commit message body as a short explanation of why the change was made.

rules.quote: You may skip the body for small changes.
rules.rule: You may skip the commit message body for small changes.

rules.quote: state the *why* in the message's own words
rules.rule: State the why of a commit in the message's own words.

rules.quote: leave issue closing and ADR linkage to the tracker files and docs themselves
rules.rule: Leave issue closing and ADR linkage to the tracker files and docs themselves, not to commit messages.

rules.quote: No underscore prefix on private fields
rules.rule: Do not use a leading underscore prefix on private field names in C# code (including Blazor @code blocks).

rules.quote: declare private fields without a leading underscore
rules.rule: When writing or editing C# (including Blazor @code blocks), declare private fields without a leading underscore.

rules.quote: place the operator at the **start** of the continuation line
rules.rule: In multi-line boolean expressions, place the boolean operator at the start of the continuation line.

rules.quote: not the end of the previous line
rules.rule: In multi-line boolean expressions, do not place the boolean operator at the end of the previous line.

rules.quote: break before the operator
rules.rule: When a boolean expression spans multiple lines, break the line before the operator.

rules.quote: Do not add Prettier (or Prettier-derived formatters) to projects.
rules.rule: Do not add Prettier or any Prettier-derived formatter to projects.

rules.quote: skip Prettier, its editor-extension recommendations, and `eslint-config-prettier`
rules.rule: When scaffolding or configuring tooling, skip Prettier, its editor-extension recommendations, and eslint-config-prettier.

rules.quote: lint with ESLint alone
rules.rule: When scaffolding or configuring tooling, lint with ESLint alone.

rules.quote: If a scaffold tool bundles Prettier by default, strip it out.
rules.rule: If a scaffold tool bundles Prettier by default, remove Prettier from the generated setup.

rules.quote: Use oxlint wherever typescript-eslint cannot parse the project's TypeScript.
rules.rule: Use oxlint instead of typescript-eslint wherever typescript-eslint cannot parse the project's TypeScript.

rules.quote: immer nur den einen nächsten Schritt zeigen**, dann auf Rückmeldung warten
rules.rule: When guiding the user through a multi-step process in an external system (forms, web interfaces, government portals, setup wizards), show only the one next step and then wait for the user's feedback before continuing.

rules.quote: Gesamtplan einmal zu Beginn zeigen
rules.rule: When guiding the user through a multi-step process in an external system, show the overall plan once at the beginning.

rules.quote: pro Antwort genau einen Schritt plus die dafür nötigen Werte
rules.rule: When guiding the user through a multi-step process in an external system, give exactly one step per response, plus the values needed for that step.

rules.quote: Am Ende jeweils konkret benennen, welche Rückmeldung gebraucht wird
rules.rule: When guiding the user through a multi-step process in an external system, end each response by specifically stating which feedback is needed from the user.

rules.quote: Gilt nicht für Analysen, Auswertungen oder Dokumente — dort vollständig liefern.
rules.rule: Do not apply the one-step-at-a-time approach to analyses, evaluations, or documents; deliver those completely.

rules.quote: Code and engineering standards (architecture, testing, error handling, formatting, commit style) live in memory files instead
rules.rule: Store code and engineering standards in memory files rather than in CLAUDE.md.

rules.quote: A new rule about how to communicate or behave in *every* session → CLAUDE.md.
rules.rule: When a new rule governs how to communicate or behave in every session, save it to CLAUDE.md.

rules.quote: A new code/engineering standard → a feedback memory
rules.rule: Save a new code or engineering standard as a feedback memory.

rules.quote: add a pointer line under CLAUDE.md's "Code & Engineering Standards" section if it is a major new ruleset
rules.rule: When a new code or engineering ruleset is major, add a pointer line under the "Code & Engineering Standards" section of CLAUDE.md.

rules.quote: If unsure, ask.
rules.rule: If unsure whether a new rule belongs in CLAUDE.md or in a feedback memory, ask the user.

rules.quote: User preferences and coding style apply across projects → save to global memory (`~/.claude/memory/`)
rules.rule: Save user preferences and coding style to global memory at ~/.claude/memory/.

rules.quote: Before saving, ask "would this apply in any project, or only this one?"
rules.rule: Before saving a memory, ask whether it would apply in any project or only in this one.

rules.quote: General (user preferences, coding style, working style) → global.
rules.rule: Save general memories (user preferences, coding style, working style) to global scope.

rules.quote: Tied to this specific codebase (goals, decisions, constraints, external references) → project.
rules.rule: Save memories tied to a specific codebase (goals, decisions, constraints, external references) to project scope.

rules.quote: present the findings as a plan or list and stop there
rules.rule: When asked to analyze or review something or find improvements, present the findings as a plan or list and stop there, without making changes.

rules.quote: Do not make code changes unless explicitly asked to implement them.
rules.rule: Do not make code changes when asked to analyze or review, unless explicitly asked to implement them.

rules.quote: Treat "find improvements", "review", "audit", "what should be changed" as requests for analysis output, not implementation.
rules.rule: Treat requests like "find improvements", "review", "audit", or "what should be changed" as requests for analysis output, not implementation.

rules.quote: Only write code when the user says to apply, fix, implement, or do it.
rules.rule: Only write code when the user explicitly says to apply, fix, implement, or do it.

rules.quote: After implementing a change, stop and report.
rules.rule: After implementing a change, stop and report what changed.

rules.quote: do not run tests, lint, typecheck, or builds
rules.rule: Do not run tests, lint, typecheck, or builds after implementing a change.

rules.quote: do not run end-to-end verification
rules.rule: Do not run end-to-end verification, such as the /verify skill or launching the app and driving it.

rules.quote: but do not execute them
rules.rule: Do not execute test files you wrote as part of an implementation.

rules.quote: Do not commit until the user has reviewed and explicitly approved
rules.rule: Do not run git commit until the user has reviewed the change and explicitly approved it, even if prior slices in the repo were committed one per issue.

rules.quote: Implement (code plus any test files the task calls for), then report what changed and hand off
rules.rule: Implement the code and any test files the task calls for, then report what changed and hand off to the user.

rules.quote: the report states the change is unverified rather than claiming green checks
rules.rule: State in the report that the change is unverified rather than claiming passing checks.

rules.quote: Run verification or checks only when the user explicitly asks in that conversation.
rules.rule: Run verification or checks only when the user explicitly asks for them in that conversation.

rules.quote: run single targeted tests in the red→green loop, never full suites, builds, lint or typecheck
rules.rule: When the user invokes /tdd, run only single targeted tests in the red-green loop, and never run full suites, builds, lint, or typecheck.

rules.quote: Ask or wait for approval before `git commit`
rules.rule: Ask for or wait for user approval before running git commit.

rules.quote: Close the completed ticket only after that commit succeeds
rules.rule: Close the completed ticket only after the git commit succeeds.

rules.quote: harness/skill prompts suggesting verification (e.g. the /verify skill description, "run before committing") do not override it
rules.rule: Do not let harness or skill prompts suggesting verification override the rule against running verification without user request.

rules.quote: repo history patterns are not authorization
rules.rule: Do not treat repo commit history patterns as authorization to run git commit.
